risks.Risk Description: Risk of cyber attacks including state-sponsored incidents, ransomware attacks, and breaches due to inadequate IT controls and a fragmented, devolved technology environment.

Risk Driver.Driver Description: Many institutions have historically not invested significantly in technical IT controls and dedicated cyber security staff.
A piecemeal build-up of systems and widespread shadow IT increases attack surfaces and reduces central oversight.
Recruiting skilled cyber security staff is challenging and costly.
Obtaining insurance to transfer part of the cyber security risks is increasingly difficult.

Risk Recommendations: Invest in robust technical IT controls and dedicated cyber security staffing
Enhance visibility and centralization of IT systems to mitigate shadow IT risks
Adopt a comprehensive cyber security strategy that includes advanced threat detection
Explore obtaining cyber security insurance where possible
risks.Trend: Cyber security has remained a top risk for three consecutive years, with increasing average impact scores and heightened concerns over state-sponsored attacks.
risks.Likelihood: High (100% occurrence in risk registers and increasing external threats)
risks.Impact: Could disrupt operations, damage reputation, and affect financial stability through significant breaches or system downtime.
Contextual Variations: Risk exposure is heightened in institutions with highly devolved IT models
Variations depend on the maturity of cyber security investments across departments

risks.Risk Description: Risk that institutions may fail to meet Net Zero targets due to challenges reducing emissions, funding constraints, and reliance on outdated estate infrastructure.

Risk Driver.Driver Description: Difficulty in obtaining funding for carbon reduction plans and sustainability investments.
Challenges in gaining organization-wide support for sustainability initiatives.
Many institutions operate old buildings not designed with sustainability in mind.
Difficulty in quantifying, monitoring, and reporting scope three emissions from areas like student travel and supply chains.

Risk Recommendations: Invest in and plan comprehensive carbon reduction initiatives
Re-assess and upgrade estate infrastructure to improve sustainability
Develop and centralize sustainability governance structures
Consider diversifying energy sources, including options for self-generation and green energy supplies
risks.Trend: Newly included in the top five risks in 2022/23, reflecting increasing external and regulatory attention.
risks.Impact: Failure to achieve Net Zero targets can harm reputation and operational sustainability.
Contextual Variations: Risk severity varies based on the age and sustainability readiness of campus estates
Differences in central sustainability governance impact overall risk exposure

risks.Risk Description: Risk arising from rising operational costs—such as energy, inflation, staff, and pension expenses—coupled with flat revenue streams and capped tuition fees.

Risk Driver.Driver Description: Increases in energy costs, inflation on non-pay expenses, and higher staff costs driven by the cost of living crisis.
Undergraduate tuition fee caps (e.g., fixed at £9,250) limit income growth despite rising student demand.
Growing international competition for students impacts enrollment and revenue generation.
Rising pension expenses add further pressure on financial sustainability.

Risk Recommendations: Conduct granular analysis of cost drivers and income streams
Identify and develop new income opportunities
Reassess investment decisions and consider bold actions such as course closures
Enhance controls over procurement, contracts, and budget performance
risks.Trend: Increasing financial pressures are evident and are reflected in 100% of risk registers.
risks.Impact: May lead to an inability to invest in strategic initiatives, risk breaches of bank covenants, and long-term financial instability.
Contextual Variations: This risk is particularly acute in markets with tuition fee caps and high operational cost pressures, such as in the UK.

risks.Risk Description: Risk linked to outdated physical estates and digital infrastructure that are misaligned with modern, blended educational delivery models.

Risk Driver.Driver Description: Historic lack of planning and investment, worsened by pandemic-induced disruptions.
The need to remodel campus layouts and repurpose spaces to support new learning and working models.
High costs and technical difficulties in moving to the cloud and integrating modern digital systems.

Risk Recommendations: Develop data models to assess current physical space usage and inform strategic decisions
Invest in upgrading and repurposing estate facilities to better match current needs
Drive investment in digital infrastructure to support blended learning and operational efficiency
risks.Trend: Infrastructure risk has increased significantly in 2022/23 as demands for both physical and digital capabilities evolve.
risks.Likelihood: High (noted across multiple registers, with some aspects at 100% occurrence)
risks.Impact: Inadequate infrastructure can adversely affect student experience, teaching quality, and overall operational efficiency.
Contextual Variations: Risk varies with the level of institutional investment and the age of campus facilities
Different institutions face unique challenges based on their digital maturity and physical estate conditions

risks.Risk Description: Risk stemming from challenges in attracting and retaining high-caliber academic and professional staff, leading to increased workloads and potential industrial action.

Risk Driver.Driver Description: Difficulty recruiting diverse, high-caliber staff in a competitive market.
Increased workloads and dissatisfaction contribute to turnover and the risk of prolonged industrial action.
Insufficient support for staff mental and emotional health exacerbates retention issues.

risks.Trend: Consistently noted in 100% of risk registers with growing concerns evidenced by recent industrial action.
risks.Impact: Can lead to prolonged industrial action, diminished student experience, and reduced organizational and financial resilience.
risks.Risk Event: Industrial action taken by thousands of staff in recent months
Contextual Variations: The risk may vary by institution size and disciplinary focus, though it remains a top concern across the sector.

risks.Risk Description: Risk associated with the volatility of student recruitment driven by shifting student priorities, changing demographics, and increased international competition.

Risk Driver.Driver Description: Unpredictable fluctuations in undergraduate applications and changes in student preferences.
Increased global competition and shifting immigration policies affecting international student flows.
A decline in Chinese student numbers offset by growth in Indian, Nigerian, French, and Italian cohorts.

risks.Trend: Mixed trends: overall international applications have grown, but key cohorts (e.g., Chinese students) are declining.
risks.Impact: Failure to meet recruitment targets can lead to reduced tuition revenue and an increased reliance on budget contingencies.
Contextual Variations: Variations are evident by country of origin and sensitivity to changes in international policy and economic conditions.

risks.Risk Description: Risk arising from challenges in maintaining a high-quality student experience amidst a shift toward digital and hybrid learning models, with implications for academic outcomes and institutional reputation.

Risk Driver.Driver Description: Reduced on-campus engagement and challenges in effectively supporting students in a blended learning environment.
An increasing number of students experiencing mental health issues, which can adversely affect satisfaction and wellbeing.

Risk Recommendations: Review and adapt support systems to identify and assist students in digital learning contexts
Reconfigure institutional processes to ensure student experience remains a priority under hybrid delivery models
risks.Trend: Although student experience risks have dropped out of the top five in impact and likelihood, they remain the most commonly reported risk in registers.
risks.Impact: Impairs academic achievement, student wellbeing, and can negatively influence student satisfaction surveys and institutional reputation.
Contextual Variations: Risk exposure may differ depending on the balance between on-campus and digital delivery models

risks.Risk Description: Risk arising from a failure to anticipate and respond to shifts in government and educational policy, potentially impacting student recruitment and strategic objectives.

Risk Driver.Driver Description: Inability to adapt to changes in UK government and Department for Education policies that influence higher education strategy.
Increasing regulatory and compliance demands that can overburden executive management.
Emerging trends such as a shift toward vocational education and lifelong learning entitlement.

risks.Trend: There is reduced concern about the political landscape compared to previous years, yet policy risks remain significant.
risks.Impact: May affect national and global student recruitment and disrupt alignment with regional economic and strategic goals.
Contextual Variations: Influence of risk varies by geographic region and local government priorities

risks.Risk Description: Risk related to the failure to strengthen research culture, forge strategic partnerships, and secure sufficient funding, thereby undermining research quality and reputation.

Risk Driver.Driver Description: Inability to recruit and retain high quality research staff and build a robust research environment.
Insufficient research grant funding and potential changes to funding rules that affect financial support for research.
Failure to establish strong national and international research partnerships that are vital for impactful work.

risks.Impact: Could result in reduced research output, loss of reputation, and financial unsustainability in research activities.
